before.title: 2.7L EcoBoost Excessive Oil Consumption from Faulty Valve Guides
before.description: 2016-2017 Lincoln MKX models with the 2.7L EcoBoost V6 (engines built roughly April 2016 to January 2017) can suffer excessive oil consumption caused by defective cylinder head valve guides that let oil seep into the combustion chamber and burn off. Owners report burning roughly a quart every 3,000 miles, often accompanied by rough idle, misfires, and blue/white exhaust smoke. Ford addressed this in Technical Service Bulletin 19-2243, whose official remedy is replacement of both left and right cylinder heads. Fouled spark plugs from oil contamination commonly trigger cylinder-specific misfire codes.
before.solution: Have the dealer confirm coverage under TSB 19-2243; the corrective procedure replaces both cylinder heads (and typically spark plugs). Monitor oil level frequently between services and document consumption to support a warranty/goodwill claim.
symptoms: excessive oil consumption (1 quart per ~3000 miles)

proposal.title: 2.7L EcoBoost Excessive Oil Consumption from Faulty Valve Guides
proposal.description: Ford TSB 19-2243 applies to certain 2016-2017 Lincoln MKX vehicles with the 2.7L EcoBoost engine built from April 1, 2016 through January 1, 2017. It documents white or blue exhaust smoke, rough idle at operating temperature or after a hot restart, misfire or an illuminated malfunction indicator, and oil consumption of 1 quart in less than 3,000 miles. Applicable DTCs are P0300-P0306, P0316, P0524 and P06DD. Ford states that valve guides may be the cause and directs technicians to replace the cylinder heads after confirming all bulletin criteria.
proposal.solution: Have a Ford or Lincoln dealer confirm the build date, 2.7L engine and symptoms against TSB 19-2243 before authorizing the repair. The bulletin procedure replaces the cylinder heads and includes a critical four-stage crankshaft-pulley-bolt torque procedure; it does not tell every 2016-2017 owner to replace spark plugs or promise warranty coverage. Check the oil level as the owner manual directs and avoid driving with low oil pressure. Do not buy cylinder heads, a gasket kit, spark plugs or a universal engine kit from this page; no universal retail part is recommended because this is a dealer/technician procedure, and exact parts and coverage must be confirmed by VIN.
symptoms: oil consumption of 1 quart in less than 3,000 miles
rough idle at operating temperature or after a hot restart

before.title: MKX 3.7L Duratec Internal Water Pump Failure
before.description: The 3.7L Duratec V6 in 2011-2018 MKX uses the same internal (timing-chain-driven) water pump design as the 3.5L Duratec. When the seal fails, coolant flows directly into the oil sump. Symptoms identical to the 3.5L pattern: milky oil, low coolant with no external leak, eventual bearing damage.
before.solution: Same job as the 3.5L — internal water pump replacement requires removal of the front timing cover. $1,500-$2,500 at independent. Replace timing chain set proactively at the same time if mileage > 100,000 — saves a second labor charge later.

proposal.title: MKX 3.7L Duratec Internal Water Pump Failure
proposal.description: This indexed page overlaps another MKX water-pump page, but neither is being removed or redirected in this proposal. The complete 447-document MKX manufacturer-communication inventory does not establish a model-wide 2011-2018 3.7L water-pump failure rate, a universal mileage threshold or a preventive timing-chain replacement rule. Ford owner guides instead say repeated coolant loss of about 1 quart or 1 liter per month requires inspection and warn that low coolant can cause overheating and engine damage. Unexplained coolant loss or fluid contamination is a diagnosis prompt, not proof that the internal pump failed.
proposal.solution: If the engine overheats, stop safely, switch it off and let it cool. Never remove the coolant-reservoir cap while the engine is running or hot. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and the engine oil inspected so the actual leak path and any contamination are confirmed before parts are ordered. Do not buy a water pump, timing-chain set or universal cooling kit from this page; no universal retail part is recommended, and the repair path and parts must be confirmed for the VIN and diagnosed cause.

before.title: Battery Cable Chafing Causing Electrical Short / Fire (Recall 19V809 / 19S41)
before.description: NHTSA recall 19V809 (Ford reference 19S41) affects 2016-2017 Lincoln MKX vehicles equipped with the 3.7L V6 engine. A battery cable can rub against the transmission shifter cable bracket, wearing through the insulation and creating an electrical short that can cause wiring to melt or overheat and increase fire risk. Ford acknowledged it was aware of three vehicle fires potentially related to the defect. About 54,000 U.S. vehicles built at the Oakville plant were covered.
before.solution: Have the dealer perform recall 19S41: remove the battery harness clips and elbow guide and install a wire-channel shield and protective sleeve over the battery cable harness, free of charge. Confirm completion via VIN lookup at NHTSA.gov.

proposal.title: Battery Cable Chafing Causing Electrical Short / Fire (Recall 19V809 / 19S41)
proposal.description: Ford safety recall 19S41/NHTSA 19V809 covers 54,411 certain 2016-2017 Lincoln MKX vehicles with the 3.7L engine, built November 12, 2014 through September 11, 2017. The B+ battery cable harness can contact the transmission shifter-cable bracket; reduced clearance can wear through insulation and short the cable to ground, increasing the risk of overheated or melted wiring or fire. Ford reviewed three 3.7L MKX underhood-fire reports, but the inspections had not identified a source for those fires.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for 19S41/19V809. The free dealer remedy removes four battery-harness clips and one elbow guide, then installs a wire-channel shield, protective sleeve, push pins and tie straps. The official filing lists no advance warning, so absence of a warning light does not prove the cable is safe. Do not buy a battery cable, shield or harness part from this page because this is a VIN-scoped, no-charge dealer recall remedy.

before.title: Internal Water Pump Failure Contaminating Engine Oil (3.5L/3.7L V6)
before.description: First-generation MKX models with the 3.5L and 3.7L Duratec/Cyclone V6 use an internal water pump driven off the timing chain inside the engine. When the pump's bearing or seal fails, coolant leaks internally into the oil rather than externally, often with little warning. The result is milky oil on the dipstick/fill cap and, if undetected, coolant-contaminated oil that destroys bearings and scores cylinder walls, leading to engine failure. Repair is labor-intensive (20-30 hours) because the timing cover must be removed, and timing chain/guides are typically serviced at the same time.
before.solution: Watch for milky oil, coolant loss without external leaks, or a weep hole drip. Replace the internal water pump (and inspect/replace timing chain and guides) at the first sign of contamination before bearing damage occurs. Address promptly to avoid total engine replacement.
symptoms: milky/frothy oil on dipstick or fill cap

before.title: MyLincoln Touch / SYNC Touchscreen Freezing and Crashing
before.description: 2011-2013 Lincoln MKX models equipped with the MyLincoln Touch (MyFord Touch) system are widely reported to freeze, go black showing 'audio off,' lag on input, and reboot while driving. Ford published bulletins in September 2011 and July 2012 acknowledging the issues but noting fixes only 'temporarily restore function.' Owners of 2013 models also report the capacitive front control panel (touch sliders/buttons) behaving erratically, with the radio or A/C turning on and off by itself. The system's reliability problems were significant enough to drag down the vehicle's overall quality ratings.
before.solution: Install the latest SYNC/MyLincoln Touch software update at a dealer; a master reset (or disconnecting the battery for a few minutes) often temporarily restores function. Persistent capacitive control-panel faults may require APIM module or control-panel replacement.
symptoms: radio or A/C cycling on and off by itself

proposal.title: MyLincoln Touch / SYNC Touchscreen Freezing and Crashing
proposal.description: Ford TSB 13-8-2 covers some 2011-2013 MKX vehicles with MyLincoln Touch that may have navigation, voice-recognition, call-sound, phone-pairing, clock, media, Wi-Fi pass-code or general system-performance concerns. Its action is a software update after checking OASIS for open field-service actions. Customer Satisfaction Program 12M01 separately covered certain 2011-2012 MKX vehicles and authorized APIM replacement only when Workshop Manual diagnosis identified the APIM as the causal part. proposal.solution: Record the exact symptoms and check the VIN in OASIS for applicable field-service actions before updating software. Have a technician confirm the current software level and diagnose the APIM as causal before replacing it; a reset or battery disconnect is not a durable diagnosis and can erase settings. Do not buy an APIM, touchscreen or control panel from this page because configuration and programming are VIN-specific and no universal retail part is recommended.

before.title: Panoramic Vista Roof Spontaneous Shattering
before.description: Lincoln MKX models with the panoramic Vista Roof have repeated owner reports of the glass spontaneously shattering, sometimes with a loud bang likened to a gunshot, both while parked and while driving at highway speeds. A class-action lawsuit alleges Ford used thinner, ceramic-tempered (rather than laminated) glass to save weight, and that the breakage originates from inside, contradicting Ford's claim of external impact. Ford generally does not warranty glass breakage, leaving many owners to pay out of pocket. No formal NHTSA recall has been issued specifically for the panoramic roof.
before.solution: Document the failure with photos and report it to NHTSA and Ford; pursue goodwill or class-action coverage where applicable. Replacement requires a full panoramic glass panel, typically through a glass specialist, since it is not covered by a recall.
symptoms: spontaneous breakage while parked or driving

before.title: Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Overheating and Failure on AWD Models
before.description: AWD Lincoln MKX models (first generation, 2007-2015) are prone to power transfer unit failure caused by heat from the nearby exhaust cooking the factory-fill 'lifetime' gear oil, breaking down lubrication. The PTU output shaft seals fail and leak burnt, dark gear oil on the passenger side, often accompanied by a speed-dependent whine, growl, or grinding noise and a burnt-oil smell. Left unaddressed, the unit can seize and damage the transmission. Ford issued TSB 19-2017 for dark fluid leaking from the right-side transfer case intermediate shaft seal.
before.solution: Replace the factory 'lifetime' fluid with full-synthetic 75W-140 gear oil approximately every 30,000 miles as preventive maintenance. If whining, leaking, or a burnt smell is present, replace the PTU seals or the unit before it seizes and damages the transaxle.
symptoms: dark fluid leak on passenger side

proposal.title: Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Overheating and Failure on AWD Models
proposal.description: Ford SSM 47230 says some 2007-2016 AWD MKX vehicles built on or before June 30, 2016 may produce a propane or natural-gas odor during idle or low-speed driving because excessive heat can break down PTU fluid. If the odor is confirmed at the PTU and the unit is repairable, Ford identifies idler-bearing repair kit GB5Z-7P258-A. SSM 46522 separately says that a 2013-2017 3.5L or 3.7L AWD MKX whose PTU is repaired or replaced for an internal failure must also receive a new vent hose because the hose can be contaminated. These sources do not prescribe a universal 30,000-mile fluid interval or prove that every leak, noise or AWD concern will seize the unit or damage the transmission.
proposal.solution: For a propane or natural-gas odor at idle or low speed, have the source confirmed under the Workshop Manual before the PTU is opened. For a diagnosed internal PTU failure on an applicable 2013-2017 3.5L or 3.7L AWD vehicle, the Ford communication requires the vent hose to be replaced with the PTU repair or replacement. Do not buy a PTU, seal, vent hose or GB5Z-7P258-A kit from this page; this is a dealer/technician diagnostic procedure and fitment must be confirmed by VIN and failure mode.
symptoms: propane or natural-gas odor during idle or low-speed driving

before.title: Rear Brake Jounce Hose Rupture (Recall 25V544)
before.description: NHTSA recall 25V544 covers 2016-2018 Lincoln MKX (and 2015-2018 Ford Edge) for a rear brake jounce hose that can rupture and leak brake fluid prematurely. A leaking hose causes longer brake pedal travel and increased stopping distances, raising crash risk. Ford notified owners of the safety risk via interim letters in September 2025, with the final remedy anticipated in 2026. This followed an earlier front brake hose recall (20V469) on the same platform.
before.solution: Check VIN at NHTSA.gov or with a Lincoln dealer for recall 25V544 and have the rear brake jounce hoses replaced free of charge once the remedy is available. Until repaired, watch for a soft/low brake pedal or fluid loss and inspect promptly.

proposal.title: Rear Brake Jounce Hose Rupture (Recall 25V544)
proposal.description: Ford safety recall 25S87/NHTSA 25V544 covers 84,412 certain 2016-2018 Lincoln MKX vehicles with rear brake jounce hoses that can rupture prematurely. A rupture causes a progressive brake-fluid leak; the driver may notice increased pedal travel or a red brake-fluid warning, and stopping distance can increase. Ford's updated Part 573 filing says it was not aware of accidents or injuries related to this concern as of the filing.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for 25S87/25V544 now. The updated filing says the free remedy is available through the dealer: inspect both rear jounce hoses, replace any damaged or leaking hose, and readjust hoses that pass inspection to reduce strain. Do not wait for a future remedy date. If pedal travel changes, the red brake warning illuminates or fluid is leaking, stop driving and arrange service. Do not buy F2GZ-2282-G, F2GZ-2282-H or another brake hose from this page because the no-charge remedy is VIN- and inspection-specific.

before.title: Takata Driver Airbag Inflator Explosion Risk (Recall 21V158 / 21V081)
before.description: 2007-2010 Lincoln MKX vehicles are part of the Takata airbag recall. The driver (and on some 2010 vehicles, passenger) frontal airbag inflator can explode when deployed because the ammonium-nitrate propellant degrades after long-term exposure to high humidity, heat, and temperature cycling. A ruptured inflator can spray metal fragments at occupants, causing serious injury or death. NHTSA lists affected 2007-2010 MKX models among Takata 'Do Not Drive' populations in certain conditions, making this a critical safety item.
before.solution: Check the VIN at NHTSA.gov immediately; dealers replace the affected driver-side (and applicable passenger-side) airbag inflator or module free of charge. Do not delay repair given the explosion/laceration risk.
symptoms: risk of inflator rupture on deployment
metal fragments ejected during airbag deployment

proposal.title: Takata Driver Airbag Inflator Explosion Risk (Recall 21V158 / 21V081)
proposal.description: NHTSA recall 21V158/Ford 21S12 covers 2007-2010 MKX driver-airbag inflators using calcium-sulfate-desiccated Takata PSDI-5 inflators that can degrade after long-term humidity and temperature cycling and rupture during deployment. Recall 21V081/Ford 21S05 is narrower: it applies to certain 2007 MKX vehicles whose passenger airbag was replaced under a prior recall and then later replaced during collision or service work with a potentially defective unit. A separate August 2024 Ford/NHTSA Do Not Drive warning covers unrepaired non-desiccated Takata campaigns including 16V384, 17V024, 18V046 and 19V001; it should not be inferred from 21V158 or 21V081 alone.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN immediately in both NHTSA and Ford recall lookup. If the VIN has an open recall in the August 2024 non-desiccated Takata Do Not Drive group, do not drive until the free repair is completed and arrange the towing, mobile repair or loaner support Ford offers. For an open 21V158 or 21V081 campaign, follow the current VIN-specific manufacturer notice promptly; dealer replacement or inspection is free. The official filings identify no advance warning. Do not buy an inflator, airbag module or steering-wheel part from this page because the remedy is VIN- and campaign-specific and must be dealer-administered.
symptoms: no advance warning identified before possible inflator rupture
sharp metal fragments possible during airbag deployment
